_comment: Per-rule stub ceilings (road-to-rule-stub-projection Phase 2). One exact-BPE token ceiling per rule carrying a migration pointer. SHRINK-ONLY: a rule may fall below its ceiling freely, and may not rise above it. Raising a ceiling to clear a failing check is the config-weakening move this repo blocks by construction — every raise needs a `history` entry whose `reason` is a real sentence. The ceilings are a floor-plus-residue SNAPSHOT taken at adoption, not a target: a rule at its ceiling is not thereby correct, only not worse. Regenerate with `check_rule_stub_ceiling --write-baseline`; never hand-edit the counts.

history.reason: Iron Law 3 gained the preservation test that decides WHO resolves a deferred item — a routing table plus the two council refinements that make it binding (a follow-up naming a roadmap that does not exist yet fails closed to the user; a council resolution is recorded at the item or it did not happen) and the residual limit both authoring seats named. This is obligation surface, not explanation: the table decides a route and the two refinements are the conditions under which the route is legal, so a reader who reaches only the pointer target has already made the decision. It could not move to the pointer target either — roadmap-progress-mechanics.md sits at the 16,000-char check_depth_budget ceiling in this same change, and pushing prose there reds a count ratchet whose whole job is refusing a fifth over-ceiling file. The section was condensed once before this raise (2201 -> 2117) by turning four prose paragraphs into bullets; further cutting would delete substance, which preservation-guard forbids.

One sentence, +23 tokens, and it is obligation surface rather than explanation: for CI, do not hand-write the wait loop. The mechanics went to the pointer target where this rule's own migration note already sends them (context-hygiene-mechanics gains the exit codes, the four not-settled states and the measured incident) — that move is what took the growth from +179 to +23, and the residue is the pointer itself, which cannot live in the guideline because a rule that does not name the helper is a rule nobody follows to it. The incident it encodes: a hand-written `until ! gh pr checks N | grep -q pending` exited when the API failed, because the error text contains no `pending`, and the session reported a settle that had not happened and retracted it in the next reply. The rule's neighbouring waiter law already says one waiter per condition; what it did not say is that the exit condition is the part that gets written wrong, which is why the helper is named here rather than described.

One sentence in Iron Law 1, +68 tokens, and it is obligation surface rather than explanation: `roadmap:progress` now passes `--archive`, so the law's operational meaning changed — a complete roadmap is moved by the same run instead of reported to a human, and the two exclusions a reader must know before trusting that (`--check` never archives, the PostToolUse hook never archives) are exactly the part that cannot be deferred to a pointer. The prose was NOT moved to docs/guidelines/agent-infra/roadmap-progress-mechanics.md, which is where this rule's migration note sends its mechanics, because that file has roughly a hundred characters of headroom under the 16,000-char depth ceiling and check_depth_budget is shrink-only with four files already over it — a FIFTH over-ceiling file reds, so moving 400 characters there would have traded this gate for that one. The full contract, the council record and its recorded dissent live with the code in src/agent-src/scripts/archival_sweep.ts, which is the third home and the one with room.
